card.statement:
According to a theorem of Kostant (see Theorem <<ref:W:Kostant>> below), for a regular nilpotent element $e$ in $\ga$, $\mc W_\chi$ is isomorphic to $\mc Z (\ga)$, the center of $U(\ga)$.

Let $e=E_{12} \in \gl_2$, which is regular nilpotent. Then $\m =\C
f$ with $f =E_{21}$, and $\mf p =\C e +\C E_{11} +\C E_{22}$. A direct computation shows that $E_{11} +E_{22}$ and $e +\frac14 h^2
-\hf h$ lie in $U(\mf p)^{\ad \m}$. (If we combine with Kostant's theorem, then $\W =U(\mf p)^{\ad \m}$ is the polynomial algebra generated by these two elements.)

Let $\ga =\gl_n$ and $e =J_n$ as in Example <<ref:W:ex:regular>>. Let

\begin{equation*}
\Omega(u) := \left(
\begin{array}{cccccc}
E_{11}+u+ 1 & E_{12} &  &\cdots & E_{1n}\\
1&E_{22}+u+ 2&E_{23}&&\vdots\\
0& &\ddots&\ddots & \vdots \\
\vdots&& \ddots & \ddots
&E_{n-1,n}\\
0&\cdots&0&1&E_{nn}  +u+ n
\end{array}
\right)
\end{equation*}

The row determinant of a matrix $A = (a_{i,j})_{n \times n}$ with non-commutative entries is defined to be

\begin{equation}
\text{rdet} \, A  = \sum_{\pi \in S_n} \text{sgn}(\pi) a_{1,\pi 1}
\cdots a_{n,\pi n}.
\end{equation}

Write $\text{rdet} \, \Omega(u) =u^n +\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i u^{n-i}$ for $w_i \in U(\mf p)$. As shown in <<cite:BK1>>, $w_i,
1\le i\le n$ are commuting elements which lie in $U(\mf p)^{\ad
\m}$, and they freely generate $\W = U(\mf p)^{\ad \m}$.
card.label: Example 19

paper.title: Nilpotent orbits and finite $W$-algebras
paper.abstract: In recent years, the finite W-algebras associated to a semisimple Lie algebra and its nilpotent element have been studied intensively from different viewpoints. In this lecture series, we shall present some basic constructions, connections, and applications of finite W-algebras.
